statement: The compact-open centralizer of a closed Polish group acting transitively on a connected second-countable surface is locally compact and acts freely and properly. Evaluation identifies it homeomorphically with the closed normalizer quotient inside the surface, and reverses multiplication. On an open orbit of the loop-generated plane group, the closure of the restriction image of the operator stabilizer is such a free proper subgroup; the restriction kernel and topology are explicitly retained.
depends_on: Gomez-Pinedo-Uzcategui, The open mapping principle for partial actions of Polish groups, Theorem 3.5; explicit sequential microtransitivity, compact-open convergence, and properness arguments; C.28 for the application
manuscript_passages: 23; folios 140–141; scans 279–281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; exact partial reduction for C.12
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None: the topology of each group and the restriction homomorphism are specified.
notes: Open evaluation supplies k_j tending to 1 with k_j x=x_j; commutation then converts convergence n_j x_j to convergence at a fixed base point. The closed evaluation image and its inverse continuity prove properness. No local continuous section, Hilbert-Smith theorem, Lie classification, or frontier-preserving contraction is assumed. Dense discrete operator images and restriction kernels are not conflated with the closed transformation group.
